codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of RL feedback controls with thumbs-up/thumbs-down buttons and noise ring indicator. The code correctly ports the old playground's RL feedback mechanism into SolidJS reactive patterns. All three validation assertions (VAL-ML-011, VAL-ML-012, VAL-JOY-004) are covered by 17 well-structured e2e tests. No blocking issues found.

issues.description: The `.then(() => {})` callback after `props.mlStore.thumbsUp()` is an empty no-op. While the comment explains that reactive signals handle updates, the empty `.then()` could be simplified to just `props.mlStore.thumbsUp()` without the `.then()` chain, or the comment could be moved to the function level. Minor style nit, not a bug.

Test VAL-JOY-004b checks that at default noise (0.05), the noise ring has 'active' class but not 'high'. This is technically correct (0.05 > 0.01 threshold), but the test name says 'noise ring is not active at default noise level' while the body asserts it IS active. The test name is misleading — it should say something like 'noise ring is active but not high at default noise'. The test body logic is correct though.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The noise ring CSS and class thresholds (0.01 for active, 0.15 for high) are magic numbers duplicated between the SolidJS component (Joystick.tsx:50-53) and the old playground (a-app.js:2697-2701). The CSS file values (3px active, 6px high) also match the old playground exactly. While this is correct porting behavior, there's no documentation of these thresholds as a shared constant or convention.

summary: Feature f09 is a clean, well-implemented port of the RL feedback controls from the old playground app. The RLButtons component provides thumbs-up/down buttons with glass morphism styling and flash feedback animations. The noise ring indicator on the joystick correctly reflects exploration noise level with 3 CSS classes (inactive/active/high) matching the old playground's exact thresholds (0.01/0.15). The ML store's thumbsUp/thumbsDown implementations use spread-aware noise caps (0.3*(1-spread) + 0.05*spread) and noise decay (0.7x on thumbs-up) correctly. 17 e2e tests cover all three validation assertions plus UI button clicks and a cross-feature flow test. One test has a misleading name (VAL-JOY-004b) but correct logic. The implementation was later extended by f10 (undo button added to RLButtons), which is expected incremental development. All tests passed (121/121) at commit time.
